bandwidth_ranges.description: Continuous analog filter widths, for hardware whose IF filter is not a discrete menu.

dc_artifact.description:
Whether the engine handles this front end's DC artifact itself. Managed hardware hides
`dc_block` and `lo_offset_hz`, which it overrides.

hardware_sweep.description:
Whether the radio sweeps in its own firmware, delivering blocks stamped with the frequency
each was taken at instead of a stream at one tuning.

sample_rate_ranges.description:
Continuous windows the radio resamples across. A radio with holes in its rate coverage —
the RTL2832U aliases between 300 kHz and 900 kHz — needs more than one, which is why this
is a list and not the single range it replaced.

DcArtifact.description:
Who places and removes the receiver's own DC artifact.

A zero-IF front end lands an impulse at the tuned frequency. Moving the LO clear of every
channel is the only correction that works, because a signal genuinely at 0 Hz is
arithmetically indistinguishable from the offset, and the blocker must not run until the
artifact has somewhere harmless to sit.

DeviceFault.description: Why a device set stopped, for the times a reader can act on it rather than only read it.

lo_offset_in_force_hz.description:
Where the LO actually sits relative to the tuned centre, which is not always what was
asked for: the front end steps it aside when a decoder is parked on the DC artifact.

values.description:
The settings this stage can actually hold, for hardware whose gain is a table rather than
an even step — the R82xx's 29 irregular entries, say. Empty means every value `range`
admits is reachable. A client renders a control that can only land on real settings, and a
driver still snaps whatever it is asked for.

HuntNode.description:
What a hunt node remembers between sessions: where it was last pointed and how loud a click
track the operator wanted.

interval_ms.description:
How often a reading is published. A hunt is walked with, so the feedback has to keep up
with the steps rather than with a status panel.

closing.description: Whether the last few readings are climbing: the answer to "warmer or colder".

floor_db.description:
The quietest and loudest this hunt has seen, so a meter can scale itself to the ground
actually covered instead of to a guess about how loud the transmitter is.

level_db.description: The strongest reading in the last interval.

smooth_db.description: The reading with the jitter taken out, which is what a walking operator can act on.

strength.description: Where the current reading sits between `floor_db` and `best_db`, from 0 to 1.

ScanMode.description: What a scan is looking for.

ScanSession.description:
The device sets sweeping one plan together, so a client can tell a ganged scan from several
unrelated ones.

hardware_sweep.description:
Whether to let a radio that sweeps in its own firmware do the sweeping. Radios without one
retune for every step either way.

margin_db.description: How far over the noise floor a carrier has to stand to be called, in close-call mode.

hardware_sweep.description:
Whether the sweep in force is the radio's own. A scan that asked for one and did not get
it says so here rather than looking like a firmware sweep that is merely slow.
